Judgment

MFA No.201561/2017 and MFA No.201562/2017 are filed by the appellant-Insurance Company aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 06.05.2017 passed in MVC No.1377/2014 and MVC No.1378/2014 on the file II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura, by which the tribunal while partly allowing the claim petitions had awarded compensation to the claimants in MVC No.1377/2014 in a sum of Rs.8,56,000/- and a sum of Rs.7,92,000/- in favour of the claimants in MVC No.1378/2014 with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petitions till realization of entire compensation amounts.
2. MFA Crob.No.200073/2017 and MFA.Crob. No.200074/2017 are filed by the claimants in MVC No.1377/2014 and MVC No.1378/2014 seeking enhancement of compensation.

When they were Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141073827/
7 proceeding on Tikota-Honawad road near the land of one Sumitra Prakash Pujari, at that time, one Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-31/1647 was wrongly parked in the middle of the road without any sign or signal.

entities.text: Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The rider of the motorcycle being unable to see the said parked Lorry had dashed to the same from behind and sustained injuries, due to which rider of the motorcycle and pillion rider died on the spot.

Thereupon, claim petitions were filed by the claimants being dependents of the deceased claiming compensation on the premise deceased Parasappa Madar Pujari aged about 38 years was carrying on agricultural work and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
Similarly, deceased Malakar S/o Laxman Natikar, aged about 48 years was carrying on agricultural - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 work and was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
and untimely death of the deceased has caused financial and emotional distress to the claimants.
(b) Respondent No.1 -the Insured of the offending Lorry and respondent No.2- the Insurer of the said lorry appeared through their counsel.

Respondent No.1 did not file written statement in MVC No.1378/2014 however filed statement in MVC No.1377/2014 denying the petition averments and also denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and contended that compensation payable if any shall be payable by the respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
(c) Respondent No.2 in both cases appeared through the counsel and filed statement of objections denying the mode and manner of accident and also contended that there was breach of terms of policy.
As such, Insurance Company was not liable to pay the compensation.
It is also contended that the rider of the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 motorcycle was riding the same in rash and negligent manner.
Hence, the Police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
The rider of the motorcycle was solely responsible for alleged accident resulting in his and pillion rider death and hence sought for dismissal of the appeal.

(d) The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence and held that accident in question had occurred on account of negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry for having parked the same in the middle of the road without there being any sign or signal or fence and consequently held that the claimants were entitled for compensation as noted above.

Being aggrieved by the same,
appellant-Insurance Company is before this Court.
4.

Sri. Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeals submits that the tribunal failed to appreciate Ex.R1 which is the sketch of - 12 - Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141073827/
8 NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 the seen of accident clearly showing that the Lorry was parked on the side of the road and the charge sheet summary clearly indicates that the rider who was riding motorcycle in rash and negligent manner had dashed the Lorry.

entities.text: Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he submits that the tribunal without appreciating these documents had come to the wrong conclusion.

5. Per contra, Sri.Sanganagouda V.Biradar, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants submits that tribunal taking into consideration of the fact that no witness has been examined with regard to seen of the accident on behalf of the appellant/Insurance Company, has come to the conclusion,
which is just and proper.
As regards the quantum of compensation is considered, learned counsel submits that tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m. which is on the lower side.
Further he submits that tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head of 'future - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 prospects' and 'other conventional heads'.
Hence, seeks for enhancement of the compensation.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
7.
The accident in question is not in dispute.
The time of the accident is about 9.30 p.m.

Perusal of the Ex.R1 reveal that width of the road is about 22 ft., and there is no material evidence produced with regard to any precaution having been taken to caution the fellow road users regarding parking of the vehicle.
Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 casts a duty on the owner or the Attender of the Lorry to park on the road side.

Considering the manner in which the vehicle has been parked and the timing of the accident which is at 9.30 p.m. it cannot be said that the rider of the motorcycle had contributed the accident and was there any negligence on the part.
The conclusion arrived at by the tribunal cannot be found fault with.
More particularly, no witness has - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 been examined on behalf of the appellant/Insurance Company with regard to the manner of the accident.
Therefore, no grounds are made out by the Insurance Company warranting interference.

Thus, appeals filed by the appellants-Insurance Company questioning the liability lacks merits and same are dismissed.
8. Adverting to the claim of the respondents/claimants with regard to the enhancement of compensation is concerned, though it is contended that deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
from his agricultural work, no income certificate has been produced in this regard.

This Court in the absence of any material evidence with regard to income takes into consideration of the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority in terms of which notional income of the victims of a road traffic accident for the year 2014 is assessed at Rs.7,500/- p.m., same is taken into consideration in these appeals also.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of - 15 - Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141073827/
9 NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 has held that certain percentage of the assessed income in the case of self-employed depending upon the age to be added to the income towards future prospects and

sentences.text: in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 the Apex Court had also held that claimants of the deceased are also entitled for compensation under the heads of 'loss of consortium' at Rs.40,000/- each.

sentences.text:
That apart the claimants would also be entitled for Rs.15,000/-
towards 'funeral expenses' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.

Claimants have also entitled for 10% towards 'other conventional heads'.
9.

The deceased -Parasappa Madar Pujari in MVC No.1377/2014 (in MFA.Crob.No.200073/2017 &
in MFA No.201561/2017) was 38 years at the time of accident as such 40% of the assessed income needs to be added - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 towards the future prospects, multiplier applicable as per chart is '15' and had left behind 5 dependents, as such 1/4th needs to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.

Calculated as above, the claimants/ respondents/cross objector would be entitled compensation towards 'Loss of Dependency' as under;
[(Rs.7,500+3,000(40% future prospects)- (1/4th towards personal and living expenses)].
Rs.10,500 X3/4 12X 15=14,17,500/-.
10.
Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', same is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'funeral expense', same is reduced to Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

The claimants/ respondents would be entitled sum of Rs.23,000/- (Rs.2,30,000+10%)
on the conventional heads.
Thus, the claimants/respondents in MFA No.201561/2017 would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,70,500/- instead of Rs.8,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Similarly, the deceased -Malakar in MVC No.1378/2014 (in MFA.Crob.No.200074/2017,
respondents in MFA No.201562/2017) was aged about 48 years as such 25% of the assessed amount needs to be added towards 'future prospects', applicable multiplier is '13' and since the deceased left behind 4 dependents, 1/3rd needs to deducted towards personal and living expenses.

sentences.text: 14. Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', same is enhanced to Rs.1,60,000/-.

The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'funeral expense', same is reduced to Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

The claimants/ respondents would be entitled a sum of Rs.19,000/-
(Rs.1,90,000+10%) on the conventional heads.
15. Thus, the claimants/respondents in MFA No.201562/2017 would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,05,875/- instead of Rs.7,92,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. With the above modification to the impugned award, MFA Crob. No.200073/2017 and MFA Crob. No 200074/2017 are allowed in part.
Appeals filed by the appellant/Insurance company are dismissed.

- 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 Compensation awarded as above shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petitions till realization.
Appellant - Insurance Company shall pay the aforesaid compensation amount within a period of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
The award of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The rider of the motorcycle being unable to see the said parked Lorry had dashed to the same from behind and sustained injuries, due to which rider of the motorcycle and pillion rider died on the spot.
Respondent No.1 did not file written statement in MVC No.1378/2014 however filed statement in MVC No.1377/2014 denying the petition averments and also denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and contended that compensation payable if any shall be payable by the respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
Hence, the Police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
The rider of the motorcycle was solely responsible for alleged accident resulting in his and pillion rider death and hence sought for dismissal of the appeal.
(d) The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence and held that accident in question had occurred on account of negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry for having parked the same in the middle of the road without there being any sign or signal or fence and consequently held that the claimants were entitled for compensation as noted above.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
As regards the quantum of compensation is considered, learned counsel submits that tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m. which is on the lower side.
Further he submits that tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head of 'future - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 prospects' and 'other conventional heads'.
Hence, seeks for enhancement of the compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 casts a duty on the owner or the Attender of the Lorry to park on the road side.
Considering the manner in which the vehicle has been parked and the timing of the accident which is at 9.30 p.m. it cannot be said that the rider of the motorcycle had contributed the accident and was there any negligence on the part.
The conclusion arrived at by the tribunal cannot be found fault with.
More particularly, no witness has - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 been examined on behalf of the appellant/Insurance Company with regard to the manner of the accident.
Therefore, no grounds are made out by the Insurance Company warranting interference.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of - 15 - Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141073827/
9 NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 has held that certain percentage of the assessed income in the case of self-employed depending upon the age to be added to the income towards future prospects and
in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 the Apex Court had also held that claimants of the deceased are also entitled for compensation under the heads of 'loss of consortium' at Rs.40,000/- each.
opennyai_summary.decision:
That apart the claimants would also be entitled for Rs.15,000/-
towards 'funeral expenses' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of estate'.
Claimants have also entitled for 10% towards 'other conventional heads'.
9.
The deceased -Parasappa Madar Pujari in MVC No.1377/2014 (in MFA.Crob.No.200073/2017 &
in MFA No.201561/2017) was 38 years at the time of accident as such 40% of the assessed income needs to be added - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 towards the future prospects, multiplier applicable as per chart is '15' and had left behind 5 dependents, as such 1/4th needs to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Calculated as above, the claimants/ respondents/cross objector would be entitled compensation towards 'Loss of Dependency' as under;
[(Rs.7,500+3,000(40% future prospects)- (1/4th towards personal and living expenses)].
Rs.10,500 X3/4 12X 15=14,17,500/-.
10.
Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', same is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'funeral expense', same is reduced to Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The claimants/ respondents would be entitled sum of Rs.23,000/- (Rs.2,30,000+10%)
on the conventional heads.
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 11.
Thus, the claimants/respondents in MFA No.201561/2017 would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,70,500/- instead of Rs.8,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
12. Similarly, the deceased -Malakar in MVC No.1378/2014 (in MFA.Crob.No.200074/2017,
respondents in MFA No.201562/2017) was aged about 48 years as such 25% of the assessed amount needs to be added towards 'future prospects', applicable multiplier is '13' and since the deceased left behind 4 dependents, 1/3rd needs to deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Seetawwa And Ors vs The Branch Manager And Ors on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141073827/
10 13.
Calculated as above, the claimants/cross objector in would be entitled compensation towards 'Loss of Dependency' as under;
[(Rs.7,500+1879(25% future prospects) - (1/4th towards personal and living expenses)].
- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 Rs.9,375 X 3/4 X12X 13=10,96,875/-.
14. Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of consortium', same is enhanced to Rs.1,60,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of estate' and a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'funeral expense', same is reduced to Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The claimants/ respondents would be entitled a sum of Rs.19,000/-
(Rs.1,90,000+10%) on the conventional heads.
15. Thus, the claimants/respondents in MFA No.201562/2017 would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,05,875/- instead of Rs.7,92,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. With the above modification to the impugned award, MFA Crob. No.200073/2017 and MFA Crob. No 200074/2017 are allowed in part.
Appeals filed by the appellant/Insurance company are dismissed.
- 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8598 Compensation awarded as above shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petitions till realization.
Appellant - Insurance Company shall pay the aforesaid compensation amount within a period of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
The award of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
